info.title: CourtMesh Public API
info.summary: Programmatic access to Indian court judgments, orders and AI case analysis.
info.description:
The CourtMesh public API exposes the same case corpus that powers courtmesh.ai:
Supreme Court of India, all High Courts, District Courts and tribunals.

## Two search engines

The API offers two distinct search endpoints and they cover different corpora:

- `POST /search/cases` runs keyword and boolean search over the full OpenSearch index of 310M+ records.
  It is fast, exact and does not consume AI credits. Use it for case numbers, party names, citations,
  judge names and exact phrases.
- `POST /search/cases/semantic` runs vector similarity search over the roughly 2M case subset that has
  embeddings. It consumes AI credits and is slower. Use it for natural language questions about legal
  concepts, fact patterns and doctrines.

## Response envelope

Every endpoint except `GET /health` wraps its payload in a standard envelope:

```json
{ "success": true, "data": ..., "meta": { ... }, "pagination": { ... } }
```

Failures inside a handler return `{ "success": false, "error": "..." }`. Failures raised by the
authentication middleware, which runs before the handler, return a bare `{ "error": "..." }` with no
`success` field. Clients should treat both as errors.

## Credits

Endpoints marked with the `ai` tag deduct AI credits from the account that owns the API key.
Keyword search, case retrieval, related documents, PDF links, judge search and timeline endpoints do not.

Most endpoints are 1 credit. The ones that are not:

| Endpoint | Credits |
|---|---|
| `GET /cases/{id}/pdf` | 5 |
| `POST /search/cases/semantic` | 10 |
| `POST /request-timeline` | 20 (1 when served from today's cached orders) |
| `POST /cases/{id}/analyze` | 100 (1 when an existing analysis is returned without re-running) |
| `POST /cases/{id}/analyze-consolidated` | 400 |
| `POST /party/screen`, matches found | 100 |
| `POST /party/screen`, no matches found | 20 |
| `POST /party/screen` with `adjudicate: true` | add 80, so up to 180 for one call |

A 402 response (`code: "INSUFFICIENT_API_CREDITS"`) carries `required`, `balance`, `shortfall` and a
`topUpUrl`. Nothing is ever charged partway: a call either completes and is billed at the price above,
or it fails and nothing is deducted.

### Free tier AI lockout

The Free tier cannot call `POST /cases/{id}/analyze`, `POST /cases/{id}/analyze-consolidated` or
`GET /cases/{id}/analysis` at all. Every one of the three refuses with `403` before any work happens
and before any credit is charged:

```json
{
  "success": false,
  "code": "API_TIER_NOT_ALLOWED",
  "message": "AI analysis is not available on the Free tier. Upgrade to generate or read case analyses.",
  "tier": "free",
  "upgradeUrl": "https://research.courtmesh.ai/api/settings/api-keys#credits"
}
```

The Free tier is a stored-records tier, not a preview of every capability at a smaller size. It has no AI
analysis (above), no semantic search (`POST /search/cases/semantic` refuses with `403`
`code: "SEMANTIC_NOT_ALLOWED"` before any work or charge, TIER_LIMITS.free.semanticSearchAllowed
is `false`), and no live court fetches (`TIER_LIMITS.free.liveFetchAllowed` is `false`: `request-timeline`
`refresh: true` refuses with `403` `code: "LIVE_FETCH_NOT_ALLOWED"`, and `analyze`'s `allowRemoteFetch: true`
refuses with the same code, both before any work or charge). What Free keeps: keyword search, case
detail, related documents, judge search, PDF links (subject to the PDF monthly cap), and
`POST /party/screen` against stored records only, deterministic scoring only (`adjudicate: true` is
`403`), capped at `10` screens a month (see "Litigation Check" below).
Upgrade to PAYG, Scale or Enterprise for AI analysis, semantic search and live fetches.

## What a record is

A "record" is any case CourtMesh has indexed from a court registry: parties, dates, disposal status and
the docket. Not every record carries the underlying order or judgment text:

- **Document bearing** records have the order or judgment text indexed. `POST /search/cases`,
  `POST /search/cases/semantic`, `GET /cases/{id}`, `GET /cases/{id}/pdf`, `POST /cases/{id}/analyze` and
  `POST /cases/{id}/analyze-consolidated` all work on document bearing records; the analyze endpoints
  fail with `400` on a record that has neither extracted text nor a stored PDF.
- **Status only** records are registry metadata with no document text yet: parties, case number, dates
  and disposal status, nothing to analyze or download. They are fully returned by
  `POST /search/cases`, `GET /cases/{id}` and `POST /party/screen`, but `hasDocuments` is `false` and
  `GET /cases/{id}/pdf` returns `404`.
- `total = documentBearing + statusOnly`. `GET /coverage` reports the split for the whole corpus and per
  court; a single case record does not carry a `recordType` field of its own, `hasDocuments` is the
  signal to read.

## Restricted records

A party can ask CourtMesh to withhold a case from search and screening under the case removal policy
(https://courtmesh.ai/case-removal-policy). This is a takedown, never a deletion: the record stays in
storage, and only its visibility through the public and API surfaces changes.

- A restricted case never appears in `POST /search/cases`, `POST /search/cases/semantic` or
  `POST /party/screen` results or in `relatedButUnverified`.
- A restricted case reached by its public case page returns `410 Gone`.
- A restricted case reached directly by `GET /cases/{id}`, `GET /cases/{id}/analysis`,
  `GET /cases/{id}/related` or `GET /cases/{id}/pdf` with its own id or case number is masked: the title
  and party names are replaced with a registry placeholder rather than the call failing outright.
- `POST /party/screen` discloses only a boolean, `coverage.someRecordsWithheld`, when a restricted case
  or a masked title was dropped from that screen. The count, the id and which candidate it was are never
  disclosed. A screen never reports `no_matches_found` on the strength of what withholding removed; see
  "Litigation Check" below for the exhaustiveness rule this follows.

## Watermarking

Three endpoints return case text with an invisible-to-the-eye watermark applied
(`server/utils/response-sanitizer-watermarked.ts`, `server/lib/robust-watermark.ts`): `GET /cases/{id}`
(title, judges, parties, disposal nature, summary), `GET /cases/{id}/analysis` (every free text field
inside `data.analysis`) and `POST /search/cases/semantic` (the same fields as `GET /cases/{id}` on each
result). The watermark works by substituting a small number of characters in the text for visually
identical Unicode homoglyphs (for example a Cyrillic О in place of a Latin O), chosen per account so a
leaked excerpt can later be traced back to the API key or user it was fetched through. Rendered or read
normally, the text looks and reads exactly the same.

**This has a real consequence for integrators: do not compare or deduplicate on watermarked text across
endpoints.** `POST /search/cases`, `POST /party/screen` and the in-app UI routes return the same
underlying fields as plain ASCII, not watermarked - so the "same" title read through `GET /cases/{id}` and
through `POST /search/cases` will not be byte-for-byte equal, and two results for the same case fetched
through two different watermarked calls (different account, different time) will not match each other
either, since the substituted characters differ per watermark. Never key equality, a hash, a regex match
or a deduplication step off a title, judge name, party name or summary string. Use the stable identifiers
instead - `id` (the case's MongoDB ObjectId) and `caseNumber` - which are never watermarked, are identical
across every endpoint, and are safe to compare, hash or use as a map key.

## Rate limits and per-IP limits

Every account has a per tier request budget enforced by `universalRateLimiter`, plus, on search
endpoints, a per tier ceiling on how much of the corpus one call or one page walk can touch:

| Tier | Requests/minute | Requests/day | Requests/month | Max page size (`limit`) | Max pagination depth |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| free | 10 | 500 | 10,000 | 20 | 1,000 |
| payg | 60 | 20,000 | 4,00,000 | 50 | 10,000 |
| scale | 120 | 1,00,000 | 20,00,000 | 100 | 50,000 |
| enterprise | 600 | 10,00,000 | 2,00,00,000 | 100 | 1,00,000 |

The per minute ceiling produces `429` with `code: "RATE_LIMITED"` and a `Retry-After` header (see the
"RateLimited" response below). The page size and pagination depth ceilings apply only to
`POST /search/cases` and `POST /search/cases/semantic`, run after request validation, and produce `400`
rather than `429` because they reject the shape of the request rather than its frequency:

- `limit` above the tier's max page size: `400` `{ "success": false, "code": "PAGE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED", "limit": ..., "tier": ... }`.
- `page * limit` above the tier's max pagination depth: `400` `{ "success": false, "code": "PAGINATION_DEPTH_EXCEEDED", "limit": ..., "tier": ... }`.

`POST /party/screen` additionally carries its own, tighter per minute ceiling on top of the tier budget
above, plus a per tier cap on distinct names screened per day (repeat screens of a name already seen
today do not count against it, only genuinely new names do) and, on the Free tier only, a monthly screen
count cap:

| Tier | party/screen requests/minute | party/screen screens/month | Distinct names/day |
|---|---|---|---|
| free | 2 | 10 | 25 |
| payg | 10 | unlimited | 500 |
| scale | 30 | unlimited | 5000 |
| enterprise | 60 | unlimited | unlimited |

Hitting the per endpoint minute ceiling or the distinct names ceiling both produce `429` with a
`Retry-After` header, `code: "RATE_LIMITED"` for the former and `code: "DISTINCT_NAMES_LIMIT_REACHED"`
for the latter. Hitting the Free tier monthly screen count produces `403`
`code: "PARTY_SCREEN_LIMIT_REACHED"`, not `429`, because it resets monthly rather than
on a rolling window.

`POST /search/cases/semantic` carries its own per tier requests-per-minute ceiling, tighter than the
account budget above, on top of the Free tier being blocked outright
(`code: "SEMANTIC_NOT_ALLOWED"`):

| Tier | semantic requests/minute |
|---|---|
| free | 0 |
| payg | 20 |
| scale | 60 |
| enterprise | 120 |

`POST /request-timeline` with `refresh: true` carries the same shape of its own ceiling, plus a per tier
daily cap on live fetches (see "Live fetches versus stored reads" below):

| Tier | timeline refresh requests/minute | live fetches/day |
|---|---|---|
| free | 0 | 0 |
| payg | 5 | 200 |
| scale | 15 | 2000 |
| enterprise | 30 | unlimited |

Two more per tier daily/monthly caps apply account-wide, both enforced by `enforceDailyCounter`
(Asia/Kolkata calendar day or month) and `withConcurrencySlot`:

| Tier | Distinct case fetches/day | PDF calls/month | Concurrent analyze jobs |
|---|---|---|---|
| free | 200 | 100 | 0 |
| payg | 5000 | 2000 | 3 |
| scale | 50000 | 10000 | 10 |
| enterprise | unlimited | unlimited | 25 |

Exceeding the distinct case fetch cap is `429` `code: "DISTINCT_CASES_LIMIT_REACHED"`;
the PDF cap is `429` `code: "PDF_LIMIT_REACHED"`; the concurrency cap on
`POST /cases/{id}/analyze` is `429` `code: "CONCURRENT_ANALYSIS_LIMIT"` with a fixed `Retry-After: 30`,
since a concurrency slot frees up quickly rather than on a fixed window. "Distinct" means genuinely new
case ids or names for that account today: repeat calls against something already counted today never
count twice.

### Per-IP limits

Two more ceilings apply per client IP address, across every account and API key that address happens to
be driving, independent of any one account's own tier budget - they exist to catch an address running many
accounts or keys, not to police a single legitimate integration:

- `300` requests per minute per IP. Exceeded: `429` `code: "RATE_LIMITED"`.
- `5` distinct API keys per IP per Asia/Kolkata day. Exceeded: `429`
  `code: "TOO_MANY_KEYS_FROM_IP"`.

Both fail open on an internal error (a broken counter store never blocks real traffic) and both are
IP address hashed before being used as a rate limit key, so no cleartext address is ever persisted in a
key name.

## Pagination cursors

`POST /search/cases` supports two ways to page past the first screen: `page` (shallow, cheap) and, for
deep pagination, a signed `cursor`. Send the previous response's `pagination.nextCursor` string back as
`cursor` on the next request; do not construct or edit one yourself. A cursor is signed
(`server/utils/signed-cursor.ts`) and carries the exact OpenSearch sort position, the paging depth reached
so far, and a hash of the query and filters that produced it, so it cannot be replayed against a different
query or hand-edited to skip past a tier's `maxPaginationDepth`. A cursor that fails to decode, or that
was issued for a different query, is refused with `400` `code: "CURSOR_INVALID"` before
any search work runs. `searchAfter` (a raw, unsigned array) is kept only for callers written before
self serve tiers existed; a self serve caller should use `cursor` instead, since an unsigned `searchAfter`
is not honoured once the tier system is live. `pagination.nextCursor` is `null` on the last page.

## Live fetches versus stored reads

Most reads on this API are served from data CourtMesh already holds. Two calls can instead trigger a
synchronous fetch from a live external source, and both are gated the same way:

- `POST /request-timeline` with `refresh: true` fetches the current order and hearing history from the
  court source system rather than serving whatever was fetched before. An explicit `refresh: false` is
  always a stored read at `meta.liveFetch: false` and the cache-hit price; state tribunal timelines are
  never live-fetchable at all (`data.liveFetchSupported: false` on the response, regardless of `refresh`),
  and a District Court timeline that was already refreshed today is throttled to once a day. Omitting
  `refresh` entirely keeps this account's legacy behaviour: with self serve tiers off (Enterprise-only
  keys today), that means the pre-tiers default of a live fetch on every call (`meta.liveFetch: true`,
  same as always) - send `refresh: false` explicitly to opt in to the stored-read contract described
  above before self serve tiers are live for this account. With self serve tiers on, omitting `refresh`
  is the same as sending `refresh: false`.
- `POST /cases/{id}/analyze` with `allowRemoteFetch: true` lets the analysis fetch its source document from
  an external host when this app holds no S3 copy, for a flat `20 credit`
  surcharge on top of the base analyze price. The target host must match `REMOTE_PDF_HOST_ALLOWLIST`
  (`server/config/api-tiers.ts`); today that is:

  - `ecourts.gov.in` (and any subdomain)
  - `sci.gov.in` (and any subdomain)
  - `hcservices.ecourts.gov.in` (and any subdomain)
  - `judgments.ecourts.gov.in` (and any subdomain)

Both refuse before any work or charge on a tier with `liveFetchAllowed: false` (Free, today) with `403`
`code: "LIVE_FETCH_NOT_ALLOWED"`, and both refuse a target host outside the allowlist with `403`
`code: "REMOTE_FETCH_NOT_ALLOWED"` regardless of tier, since that check is an SSRF/scraping guard, not an
entitlement one. See "Rate limits and per-IP limits" above for the per tier live-fetch minute and daily
ceilings that apply once a live fetch is otherwise allowed.

## IP allowlisting

An organisation may ask CourtMesh support to restrict its API keys to a fixed set of source IP addresses.
This is configured on the account by support, not through a self serve endpoint. Once enabled in strict
mode, a request from an address outside the allowlist is refused with `403` `code: "IP_NOT_ALLOWED"` before
the request reaches any handler, and before any credit is charged. Contact support to enable it or to
change the allowlisted addresses.

## Versioning and deprecation

This is `v1` of the API, named in the base path (`/api/v1/prod`). Within `v1`, changes are additive only:
a new field, endpoint or error code is fair game; removing or renaming an existing field, changing a
field's type, or tightening a previously permissive validation are all breaking and reserved for a future
version. A field a client does not recognise should always be ignored, never treated as an error.

A breaking change to an existing `v1` behaviour is announced at least 90 days ahead on the changelog at
<https://courtmesh.ai/indian-court-cases-api/changelog>, and the affected responses carry a `Deprecation`
header (a date, RFC 3339) and, once a replacement is ready, a `Sunset` header (the date the old behaviour
stops working) until the change actually ships.

## Data licence and caching

This API grants a licence to retrieve and display CourtMesh data for your own use; it is not a licence to
redistribute, resell or bulk republish the corpus as your own dataset. Cache a raw record you fetched for
up to 30 days before re-fetching it; do not build a second, independently updated copy of the corpus.
When you display a record to an end user, attribute it: "Source: CourtMesh". See
<https://courtmesh.ai/terms> for the full terms.

## Security

All traffic is served over TLS. API keys are hashed at rest (never stored or logged in plaintext) and
compared with a constant-time check. All infrastructure is hosted in India. A Data Processing Agreement is
available on request for enterprise accounts (contact support). CourtMesh does not hold a SOC 2 report
today.

## Limits

Request bodies are capped at 256 kb (`413` `code: "PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE"` beyond that). Malformed JSON is
`400` `code: "MALFORMED_JSON"`. `POST /search/cases/semantic` allows up to 10 minutes for a single call;
every other endpoint is expected to complete well inside a minute, with `POST /search/cases` itself
bounded to a 90 second upstream budget (`408` `code: "UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT"` past that).

## CORS

This API is meant to be called server side. It does not set permissive CORS headers for the keyed
endpoints (unlike `GET /coverage` and `GET /reference/*`, which are public and do set them), so a browser
calling it directly from a page will be blocked by the browser's own CORS check regardless of the key's
validity. Never embed an API key in client side JavaScript shipped to a browser; proxy the call through
your own backend instead.

`GET /coverage`, `GET /reference/courts` and `GET /reference/case-types` all use the same allowlist:
`courtmesh.ai` and any origin configured for the marketing site get their own `Origin` reflected back in
`Access-Control-Allow-Origin`; any other caller, including a bare curl request with no `Origin` header at
all, still gets a usable value rather than being refused, since the data behind all three is public and
identical for every caller regardless of origin. Each also sends `Vary: Origin`.

## Request ids and errors

Every response, success or failure, carries an `X-Request-Id` header: either the value you sent in your
own `X-Request-Id` request header (if it matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,128}$`) or a freshly generated one.
Quote it in a support ticket to let CourtMesh join your report to the exact server side log line.

A refusal raised inside a route handler (`sendApiError`, `server/utils/api-error.ts`) uses one shared
envelope:

```json
{ "success": false, "code": "CASE_NOT_FOUND", "message": "Case not found", "error": "Case not found", "requestId": "..." }
```

`error` mirrors `message` for callers written against the older bare `{ error }` bodies. `requestId` is
the same value as the `X-Request-Id` response header, repeated in the body for a client that only reads
JSON.

**Not every refusal on this API goes through that one function**, and the ones that do not carry a
narrower body, documented here rather than pretended away:

- The per tier query-shape guard on `POST /search/cases`/`POST /search/cases/semantic`
  (`PAGE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, `PAGINATION_DEPTH_EXCEEDED`, `CURSOR_INVALID`) sends `{ success, code, limit,
  tier }` (or, for `CURSOR_INVALID`, `{ success, code, message }`) directly rather than through
  `sendApiError`: still no `message`/`error` on the first two, but `requestId` IS included (2026-09-18
  fix) whenever the request-id middleware had already run - the field is simply omitted when it had not.
- The self serve per tier/per endpoint/distinct-count/concurrency limiters
  (`server/utils/rate-limiter.ts`: the per tier minute/day/month budget, `POST /party/screen`'s own
  minute ceiling, the distinct-names/distinct-case/PDF/live-fetch daily counters, and the analyze
  concurrency gate) send `{ success, error, code, message, retryAfter, resetTime }` directly. As of the
  same 2026-09-18 fix these also include `requestId` whenever the request-id middleware had already run
  (omitted otherwise) - the older, flag-independent per-key/per-JWT limiter (`RATE_LIMITED` via
  `sendApiError`) always carried one already.
- `GET /me` and `GET /audit` now go through `sendApiError` (2026-09-18 fix) with `code: "API_KEY_INVALID"`
  (account resolution), `code: "USER_NOT_FOUND"`, `code: "FORBIDDEN_SCOPE"` (organisation/user scope
  refusals) or `code: "INTERNAL_ERROR"`, so they carry the same `{ success, code, message, error,
  requestId }` shape as every other route handler refusal.

## Idempotency

Send an `Idempotency-Key` request header on `POST /party/screen`, `POST /party/screen/batch`,
`POST /cases/{id}/analyze`, `POST /cases/{id}/analyze-consolidated` or `POST /request-timeline` to make a
retried call safe. The key is scoped to your API key id and is remembered for 24 hours. "The same
request" means the same method, path and request body (object key order does not matter).

- With no `Idempotency-Key` header at all, this is a total no-op: behaviour is byte for byte unchanged.
- A first use of a key runs the handler normally.
- A retry with the SAME key, while the first call is still in flight, is refused with `409`
  `code: "IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS"` rather than started a second time.
- A retry with the same key AFTER the first call finished with a 2xx replays that original response
  verbatim (same status code and body) with an `Idempotency-Replayed: true` response header, and is not
  charged again. A first call that did NOT finish 2xx is never stored as a replay candidate at all, so a
  retry after a failure is simply treated as a fresh first use of the key.
- The same key reused for a DIFFERENT request is refused with `409` `code: "IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED"`,
  since a key's whole point is to identify one specific call.
- A key that does not match `^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,128}$` is refused with `400`
  `code: "IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INVALID"` before any work happens.
- For `POST /party/screen` and `POST /party/screen/batch` specifically, a replay returns `data.query`
  (or, for the batch endpoint, each item's `screen.query`) with `name`/`aliases` redacted to lengths
  rather than the original searched values, even though the first (non-replayed) call returns them in full.

Idempotency is optional: a call with no `Idempotency-Key` header behaves exactly as it does today, with no
replay protection.

get.description:
Case insensitive substring search over the combined Supreme Court and High Court judge name lists.

Use this to resolve the exact spelling of a judge name before passing it as the `judgeName` filter to
`POST /search/cases`. Results are always capped at 50 names. Omitting `q`, or passing an empty `q`,
returns the first 50 names of the combined list rather than an error.

Does not consume AI credits.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Substring to match against judge names, case insensitive. Omit or leave empty to get the first 50 names.

200.description: Matching judge names, capped at 50.

post.summary: Keyword search across all Indian court cases
post.description:
Keyword and boolean search over the full OpenSearch index of 310M+ Indian court records.
Fast, exact and free of AI credit cost.

Prefer this endpoint over `POST /search/cases/semantic` for case numbers, citations, party names,
judge names and exact phrases. Use the semantic endpoint for conceptual questions.

### Pagination

For the first few pages use `page`. For deep pagination send the previous response's
`pagination.nextCursor` string back as `cursor`; see "Pagination cursors" above for what it carries
and why it cannot be hand constructed. `searchAfter` (a raw, unsigned array) is kept only for callers
written before self serve tiers existed; a self serve caller should use `cursor` instead.
`pagination.nextCursor` is a `string | null`: a string while more pages exist, `null` on the last page.

### Sorting

`sortBy` accepts `relevance` (default), `recent` (newest decision date first) and `oldest`.
`date` is a deprecated alias for `recent`: it is still accepted, and the response carries a
`meta.warnings` entry telling you what it was applied as. `meta.sortBy` always reports the sort that
was actually used.

### Filter notes

- `caseNumber` filters on the exact case number. The search service takes a single value, so an array
  with more than one entry is rejected with 400 rather than silently truncated.
- `judgeName`, `judges` and `judge` are three aliases for the same filter. The handler uses the first
  of them that is set, in that order.
- `meta.filters` reports the filters as they were applied.

### Response field allowlist

Every hit is passed through an explicit allowlist before it leaves this API, regardless of what the
search index happens to carry internally: `_id`/`id`, `caseNumber`, `cnr`, `title`, `court`,
`courtType`, `courtName`, `caseType`, `caseStatus`, `caseYear`, `decisionDate`, `registrationDate`,
`filingNumber`, `registrationNumber`, `petitioners`, `respondents`, `judges`, `citation`,
`disposalNature`, `hasDocuments`, `practiceAreas`, `precedentValue`, `summary`, `highlights`, `score`.
Anything else, including any future field added to the index, is dropped rather than served without
review.

### Restricted records on this endpoint

Every page is re-checked against the restricted-case list before it is returned (OpenSearch itself
carries no `restricted` field). `meta.someRecordsWithheld: true` means at least one hit on this page
was dropped for that reason. If the re-check itself fails, this app cannot tell which hits on the page
are safe, so nothing is dropped but every hit's `title` and party fields are replaced with a
placeholder instead, and `meta.restrictedCheckDegraded: true` is added alongside
`someRecordsWithheld: true`.

post.summary: AI semantic search over embedded cases
post.description:
Vector similarity search over the case subset that has embeddings, roughly 2M records, which is a
much smaller corpus than the keyword index. Consumes AI credits and can take a minute or more.

Before searching, the service uses a language model to pull structured filters out of the natural
language query and to rewrite the remainder into legal terminology. The top level filter parameters
override what the model extracted, and the nested `filters` object overrides both.

### Important behaviours you must code for

- **The status code reflects the outcome.** An earlier version of this handler flushed a 200 before
  doing any work, so failures arrived as HTTP 200 with a `{"success": false}` body. They no longer do:
  an embedding or vector search failure is a 502, and an unexpected failure is a 500. A search that
  ran and matched nothing is still a 200 with an empty `data` array.
- **Filters are applied where you put them.** Every top level filter parameter is mapped onto a vector
  store key and reported in `meta.appliedFilters`. Two of them are narrower than on the keyword
  endpoint because of what the vector index can express: `caseNumber` must be digits only, and only
  one judge name can be filtered per request. Both are rejected with 400 rather than dropped.
- **Filter only queries fall back to keyword search.** If the model strips the query down to fewer
  than 3 characters, the request is served by the keyword engine instead and `meta.fallbackMode` is
  set to `opensearch`.
- **`pagination.total` is an estimate.** The handler fetches one extra row to detect whether another
  page exists, so `total` and `totalPages` are exact only on the final page.
- **Restricted records are withheld the same way `POST /search/cases` withholds them.**
  `meta.someRecordsWithheld: true` means at least one hit was dropped as restricted or masked, and
  `meta.restrictedCheckDegraded: true` alongside it means the restricted-case re-check itself failed,
  so every hit on the page has its title and party fields masked as a precaution instead. See
  "Restricted records" above.

**Not available on the Free tier** (`TIER_LIMITS.free.semanticSearchAllowed` is `false`): every Free
tier call refuses with `403` `code: "SEMANTIC_NOT_ALLOWED"` before any work or
charge. Every other tier also carries its own per minute ceiling on this endpoint, tighter than the
account's general budget:

| Tier | semantic requests/minute |
|---|---|
| free | 0 |
| payg | 20 |
| scale | 60 |
| enterprise | 120 |

post.summary: Trigger AI analysis of a single case
post.description:
Starts AI analysis of one case. **Consumes AI credits.**

This is asynchronous. The normal response is `202 Accepted` with `status: "processing"`, and the work
continues in the background. Poll `GET /cases/{id}/analysis` after roughly 30 to 60 seconds.

If the case already has an analysis and `force` is false, the endpoint short circuits with `200` and
returns the existing analysis inline, with `alreadyExists: true`. Pass `force: true` to re analyse.

The background job prefers file based analysis of the stored PDFs and falls back to analysing the
extracted text. If neither the extracted text nor a PDF source is available the request is rejected
with `400` before any credit is spent. Note that credit exhaustion is detected inside the background
job, so it surfaces in server logs rather than in this response.

### Fetching a document from outside S3

When the case has no document already stored in S3 but does carry an external `pdfUrl` (or an S3 URL
this app cannot resolve to its own bucket), pass `allowRemoteFetch: true` to let the analysis fetch it
live from that host. This adds a flat `20 credit` surcharge on
top of the base analyze price, charged at admission alongside the base price rather than as a second
settlement. The target host must match `REMOTE_PDF_HOST_ALLOWLIST`; a host outside it refuses with
`403` `code: "REMOTE_FETCH_NOT_ALLOWED"` regardless of tier, and the Free tier cannot use
`allowRemoteFetch` at all (`403` `code: "LIVE_FETCH_NOT_ALLOWED"`). See "Live fetches versus stored
reads" above. Omitting `allowRemoteFetch` when it would have been needed refuses with `403`
`code: "REMOTE_FETCH_NOT_ALLOWED"` rather than silently analysing nothing.

This endpoint also enforces this tier's concurrent analyze job cap: a call made while the account
already has the tier's maximum number of analyze jobs running refuses with `429`
`code: "CONCURRENT_ANALYSIS_LIMIT"` and a fixed `Retry-After: 30`.

**Consumes 100 credits (1 when `alreadyExists: true` is returned,
plus 20 more when a remote fetch actually ran).**
On the Free tier this endpoint refuses with `403` `code: "API_TIER_NOT_ALLOWED"` before any work or
charge; see "Credits" above.

post.summary: Screen a person or company name against the case corpus
post.description:
Searches the corpus for cases naming the given person or company, resolves how likely each
candidate is to actually be that party, and returns confidence scored matches. Tagged `ai` because
the optional `adjudicate: true` pass runs a language model over the uncertain middle; the
deterministic core (name similarity, identifier matching) always runs and never calls a model.

### Pricing

A screen that finds at least one match costs 100 credits. A screen that finds
none costs only 20: the retrieval work is the same either way, but a
genuine negative did not produce anything to analyse. `adjudicate: true` adds a flat
80 credit surcharge whenever it is requested, regardless of how
many candidates actually needed the model (at most 40 per call), so the
most one call can ever cost is 180 credits. `meta.creditsCharged`
reports what actually left the wallet on this call, never a theoretical or list price; reconstruct
your bill from it rather than assuming the price table, since the no-match price applies whenever
`summary.matchCount` is 0 regardless of what you expected going in. `meta.metered` is `false` (and
`meta.creditsCharged` is always `0`) before self serve tiers are on for this account, or on an
Enterprise account even with the flag on - both are genuinely unmetered today, not merely showing a
zero balance for an unrelated reason.

### Confidence bands

Each match carries `confidence.band`, one of four values, driven by a calibrated match probability
`confidence.score` between 0 and 1:

| Band | Score | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `confirmed` | >= 0.90, or an exact statutory identifier match (PAN, GSTIN, CIN, LLPIN) | High confidence this candidate is the searched party. |
| `probable` | >= 0.70 | Strong name and context evidence, short of confirmed. |
| `possible` | >= 0.45 | Plausible but weak evidence; review before acting on it. |
| `unlikely` | below 0.45, or an identifier conflict | Shown only if it clears `displayThreshold`; usually filtered out. |

**A person is never auto-confirmed on name evidence alone.** For `entityType: "person"`, a name-only
match is capped below the `confirmed` threshold even at a perfect name similarity; the candidate can
only reach `confirmed` through an exact identifier match, or, with `adjudicate: true`, a model that
still respects the same cap on a common name with no disambiguator. This mirrors the identical rule
in CourtMesh's CLM counterparty screening, on purpose: the same name, however common, must never be
silently treated as one person across products.

`confidence.engine` is `"rules"` when the deterministic core produced the band, or `"llm"` when
`adjudicate: true` was set and the model actually reviewed that candidate (it does not run on every
candidate: only the ones the deterministic core could not already decide, capped at
40 per call, cheapest and most ambiguous first).

### The verdict and exhaustiveness

`summary.verdict` is `"matches_found"` whenever `matches` is non-empty. It is `"no_matches_found"`
ONLY when the underlying search was actually exhaustive for this name
(`coverage.exhaustive || coverage.exhaustiveWithinFilters`). Anything short of that, a plan clamp, a
strategy that errored, a merely partial run, reports `"inconclusive"` instead: an absence of matches
is never reported as an absence of litigation history unless the retrieval genuinely covered the
corpus. Read `coverage.strategiesRun`, `coverage.planClamped` and `coverage.anyStrategyErrored` to
see why a call came back inconclusive.

### Restricted records

A case withheld under the case removal policy, or one still carrying a registry masking token on its
title, is dropped before scoring and never appears in `matches` or `relatedButUnverified`.
`coverage.someRecordsWithheld` is the ONLY signal this happened: it is a plain boolean, never a count
or an id, and it does not by itself flip the verdict away from `"matches_found"` when other matches
still stand. See "Restricted records" above for the full policy.

### DPDP and logging

`purpose` is required so the caller states, per DPDP section 5 grounds, why this name is being
processed before CourtMesh does any work on it. The searched `name`, `aliases`, `knownPersons`,
`identifiers` and `address` are never written to any log or to `api_key_transactions`: only their
lengths and counts are, alongside `purpose`, `entityType`, the match count and whether adjudication
ran. This is the same data minimisation `POST /search/cases/semantic` and the internal screening
service already follow.

### relatedButUnverified

Candidates the search layer surfaced but that did not clear the scoring floor, or exist only to show
why a stronger match was preferred, are returned separately in `relatedButUnverified` with only the
plain case fields, no `confidence`, `evidence`, `partyRole` or `rationale`. Treat these as leads to
review manually, not as scored results.

post.summary: Request the live order and hearing history for a case
post.description:
Starts a job that fetches the current order and hearing history for a case from the court source
systems. Poll the returned `requestId` with `GET /get-timeline/{requestId}`.

`case_id` must be the 24 character MongoDB ObjectId of the case, which is the `id` field returned by
the search and case endpoints. A case number will not work here.

Behaviour differs by court:

- Supreme Court cases return immediately with `status: "completed"`, `orderCount: 0` and a message
  explaining that SC cases have no separate orders.
- District Court cases are fetched synchronously and come back `completed` or `failed`.
- High Court cases are queued and normally come back `pending`, so they need polling. If orders were
  already fetched today the response is served from cache with `cached: true` and the orders inline.

This endpoint has no zod schema for `case_id` itself: it is checked manually, must be present and must
be a 24 character hexadecimal id, otherwise the request is rejected with 400.

### Stored read versus live refresh

With self serve tiers on for this account, omitting `refresh` (or sending `refresh: false`) is a
stored read: it never touches a live court source, prices at the cache-hit rate
(`1` credit), and `meta.liveFetch` is `false`. Pass `refresh: true` to force
a live fetch instead.

**Before self serve tiers are live for this account (Enterprise-only keys today):** omitting `refresh`
keeps this endpoint's pre-tiers behaviour byte-for-byte, which is a live fetch on every call
(`meta.liveFetch: true`), exactly as it always was for callers that predate the `refresh` field.
Send `refresh: false` explicitly to opt in to the stored-read contract above right now; sending
`refresh: true` also behaves as documented above. In short: only an *explicit* `refresh` value is
honoured before self serve tiers are on; a request that never mentions `refresh` gets the old
always-live behaviour.

Two things can stop a live fetch from happening once one is requested:

- **State tribunal cases are never live-fetchable at all.** `data.liveFetchSupported` is `false` on the
  response regardless of `refresh`, and a `refresh: true` request against one is simply served as a
  stored read rather than erroring.
- District Court cases already refreshed once today are throttled to once a day; a second
  `refresh: true` call the same day refuses with `403` `code: "LIVE_FETCH_LIMIT_REACHED"` once the
  daily cap is reached, or `429` on the endpoint's own tighter per minute ceiling.

A tier with `liveFetchAllowed: false` (Free, today) cannot use `refresh: true` at all: it refuses with
`403` `code: "LIVE_FETCH_NOT_ALLOWED"` before any work happens, before any credit is charged, and
before the endpoint's own rate limiter runs. `20` credits are charged only when
`refresh: true` actually reached a live source; see "Live fetches versus stored reads" above.

200.description: Job accepted, or orders (stored or freshly fetched) returned inline.

liveFetch.description: Whether this call actually reached a live court source, driving the price: the cache-hit rate when false, the full price when true.

400.description: `case_id is required`, or `case_id must be a 24 character hexadecimal case id` when the value cannot be an ObjectId.

403.description:
The tier may not use `refresh: true` at all (`code: "LIVE_FETCH_NOT_ALLOWED"`), or this District
Court case was already refreshed today (`code: "LIVE_FETCH_LIMIT_REACHED"` - carried here as a 403
when it is checked as a daily entitlement rather than a rate window; see "Live fetches versus
stored reads" above), or an account level refusal (`ForbiddenError`).

the same data.

key, user or organisation id) returns the same `404` as a job that does not exist at all, rather than
confirming another account's `requestId` is real.

Tribunal, and District Court, whether answered from storage or fetched live): the `requestId` it
returns there is the case's own id, not a job id. Calling this endpoint with that id returns the same
case's stored orders directly (`status: "completed"`, `orders`, `orderCount`, `cached: true`) instead

callable straight from curl or from the public coverage page, so it sits outside the metered key
authentication every other endpoint on this page requires and outside the credit system entirely.

Backed by a 6 hour server side cache (`coverage:v1`) of a query against the OpenSearch index, with a
stale-serve fallback: an expired cache still serves its last known snapshot while a refresh is
attempted in the background, rather than blocking the request or failing it. Only a cold cache with
the source unreachable returns `503`.

`data.total = data.documentBearing + data.statusOnly`. See "What a record is" above for what those
two counts mean. `data.districtCourts` is one rolled up row rather than a row per court: the index
carries no state field to group District Courts by today.

`Cache-Control: no-store` on a `503`. CORS is permissive: `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` is set for
every caller (courtmesh.ai and any configured marketing origin get their own origin reflected back;
anyone else, including a bare curl with no `Origin` header, gets a usable wildcard-equivalent value
rather than being refused), because the data is identical and public for every caller regardless of
origin.

post.summary: Screen up to 25 people or companies in one call
post.description:
Runs `POST /party/screen` for up to 25 items in one call, with bounded
concurrency (`PARTY_SCREEN_BATCH_DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY`, 2 at a time), and returns every result together.
Not available on the Free tier at all. `adjudicate` is fixed at `false` for the whole batch:
adjudication is single-item only, on `POST /party/screen` directly.

### Request shape

`purpose` is required once at the top level and applies to every item (DPDP section 5 grounds, same as
`POST /party/screen`). `entityType` may also be given once at the top level as a default; each item
must resolve an `entityType` one way or the other (its own, or the batch default) or that item fails
validation. Each item may carry its own `clientRef` (1 to 64 characters, echoed back on its result so
you can join it to your own records without CourtMesh needing to understand your identifiers) and
otherwise takes the same fields as `POST /party/screen`'s body minus `purpose` and `adjudicate`, with
two tighter per-item ceilings: up to 3 `aliases` (a single call
allows 7) and a `limit` of at most 40 (a single call allows 100) -
batch requests are already fanning out across up to 25 items, so each
one is kept lighter than a standalone screen.

### Admission order: tier, rate, monthly cap, then distinct names

1. The Free tier is refused outright, before validation of the items even matters:
   `403` `code: "API_TIER_NOT_ALLOWED"`.
2. This endpoint shares `POST /party/screen`'s own per minute ceiling (one consumption per batch call,
   not per item).
3. The monthly party screen cap (Free is blocked above, so this applies to every other tier only when
   it is ever finite): if fewer screens remain this period than `items.length`, the WHOLE batch is
   refused with `403` `code: "PARTY_SCREEN_LIMIT_REACHED"`, carrying `limit`,
   `remaining` and `requested` alongside the usual `tier`/`upgradeUrl` - never a partial admission.
4. The distinct-screened-names-per-day cap is checked per item, IN REQUEST ORDER. The first item that
   would trip it stops admission for every item from it onward: those trailing items are simply never
   run and never appear in `data.results` at all (not even as a failure). The response is still `200`,
   with `meta.truncated: true` and `meta.truncatedReason` (a code string). `data.summary.items` counts
   only the admitted items, so it can be smaller than the request's `items.length` when this fires.

### Pricing

Each admitted item prices exactly like a single `POST /party/screen` call: 100
credits for a match, 20 for no match, and a failed item is never charged.
The pre-flight credit reservation covers `admittedCount * 100` credits (the
worst case for what will actually run, already shrunk by the distinct-names truncation above); a short
balance is `402`, the same `InsufficientApiCreditsError` shape as every other endpoint's pre-flight
gate. `meta.creditsCharged` reports what actually left the wallet, summed only over items that
actually completed - never a theoretical or list price - and is always `0` when `meta.metered` is
`false` (before self serve tiers are on for this account, or on an Enterprise account even with the
flag on).

### Per item failures do not fail the batch

An item that was admitted but then failed while actually running (a restricted-case gate issue, a
transient retrieval error) is reported as
`{ clientRef?, index, ok: false, error: { code: "PARTY_SCREEN_ITEM_FAILED", message } }` in
`data.results`, alongside every other admitted item's successful
`{ clientRef?, index, ok: true, screen }` entry. `index` is always the item's 0 based position in the
ORIGINAL request `items` array, so a result can still be matched to its request even when the
distinct-names cap above dropped some items out of the middle. The overall call still returns `200` as
long as it ran at all; `data.summary` tallies outcomes (including truncated-away items, which count
against neither `summary.items` nor any other summary field - they simply are not represented).

CourtMesh API key sent in the `X-API-Key` header.

Keys look like `cm-` followed by 32 base64url characters, a hyphen, then 4 more base64url characters.
Legacy keys issued with the `vv-` prefix are still accepted. Keys that do not match that shape are

A 24 character hexadecimal value is looked up by `_id` first, and if no document matches it is then
looked up as a case number. Anything else goes straight to the case number lookup. 404 means neither
lookup found a document.

Make a retried call safe. Scoped to your API key and remembered for 24 hours. See "Idempotency" above
for the full replay and conflict semantics.

Must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,128}$`; a value that does not is refused with `400`
`code: "IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INVALID"` before any work happens.

example.error: Idempotency-Key must be 1 to 128 characters of letters, digits, underscore, period or hyphen.

IdempotencyConflict.description:
Either the same `Idempotency-Key` was already used for a DIFFERENT request
(`code: "IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED"`), or a call with the same key is still in flight
(`code: "IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS"`). See "Idempotency" above. Neither charges credits: the original
in-flight or completed call is the only one that is, or will be, billed.

value.message: This Idempotency-Key was already used with a different request.
value.error: This Idempotency-Key was already used with a different request.

inProgress.summary: Same key, first call still running

value.message: Another request with this Idempotency-Key is still in progress.
value.error: Another request with this Idempotency-Key is still in progress.

ErrorCode.title: ErrorCode
ErrorCode.description: Every machine readable code this API can return, and the HTTP status normally paired with it. See "Request ids and errors" in the top level description for the full table and for which response shapes carry which fields.

ForbiddenError.title: ForbiddenError
ForbiddenError.description: The general purpose 403 shape, produced by `sendApiError` (`server/utils/api-error.ts`) unless noted otherwise. `callsToday`/`maxAllowed` are present only on the legacy Enterprise daily-quota and Free tier monthly-quota refusals (`buildApiRefusalResponse`, `server/config/api-tiers.ts`), which build their body directly rather than through `sendApiError` and so never carry `requestId`.

requestId.description: Absent on the legacy `callsToday`/`maxAllowed` shape; present otherwise.

code.description: Machine readable refusal code. See ErrorCode for the complete list; the ones a 403 can carry are enumerated here.

callsToday.description: Present only on the legacy `callsToday`/`maxAllowed` shape: a daily API call quota, or a monthly cap reported the same way (for example `PARTY_SCREEN_LIMIT_REACHED`).

maxAllowed.description: Present only on the legacy `callsToday`/`maxAllowed` shape.

limit.description: Present on a monthly-cap refusal such as `PARTY_SCREEN_LIMIT_REACHED` or `PDF_LIMIT_REACHED`.

remaining.description: Present only on `POST /party/screen/batch`'s monthly-cap refusal: screens left this period before the batch was even attempted.

requested.description: Present only on `POST /party/screen/batch`'s monthly-cap refusal: `items.length` from the request.

TierNotAllowedError.title: TierNotAllowedError
TierNotAllowedError.description: Refusal shape for API_TIER_NOT_ALLOWED: the Free tier calling an endpoint it has no access to at all. Distinct from ForbiddenError: it always carries `success`, `code` and `upgradeUrl`.

message.example: AI analysis is not available on the Free tier. Upgrade to generate or read case analyses.

TierCapExceededError.title: TierCapExceededError
TierCapExceededError.description: Returned by the per tier query-shape guard (server/middleware/api-tier-limits.ts), which runs after zod validation on `POST /search/cases` and `POST /search/cases/semantic`. Builds its body directly rather than through `sendApiError`: no `error` or `message` field on `PAGE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`/`PAGINATION_DEPTH_EXCEEDED` (check `code` instead); `requestId` IS included (2026-09-18 fix) whenever the request-id middleware had already run, omitted otherwise.

requestId.description: Present when the request-id middleware had already run; absent otherwise.

InsufficientApiCreditsError.title: InsufficientApiCreditsError
InsufficientApiCreditsError.description: HTTP 402. The API credit wallet does not cover this call. See the InsufficientApiCredits response for what each field means.

required.description: Credits this call would have cost.

balance.description: Wallet balance at the time of the check.

contactAdmin.description: Present instead of `topUpUrl` when the wallet is org owned and this caller is not an admin.

RateLimitError.title: RateLimitError
RateLimitError.description: Shared by every 429 on this API. The legacy per-key/per-JWT limiter and the entitlement gate's own 429s go through `sendApiError` and always carry `requestId`; the self serve per tier/per endpoint/distinct-count/daily-counter/concurrency limiters build this body directly but, as of the 2026-09-18 fix, also include `requestId` whenever the request-id middleware had already run (the field is simply omitted when it had not). See "Request ids and errors" above.

success.description: Present on every shape this API actually returns today.

code.description: The specific limiter that refused this call. See ErrorCode for the complete list.

requestId.description: Always present on the legacy per-key/per-JWT limiter and the entitlement gate's 429s. Present on a self serve per tier/per endpoint/daily/concurrency limiter body only when the request-id middleware had already run; absent otherwise.

retryAfter.description: Seconds until the window resets. Fixed at 30 for `CONCURRENT_ANALYSIS_LIMIT`.

resetTime.description: When the window resets. Absent on `CONCURRENT_ANALYSIS_LIMIT`, which has no fixed window.

ErrorEnvelope.title: ErrorEnvelope
ErrorEnvelope.description: Standard error shape produced inside a route handler via `sendApiError` (server/utils/api-error.ts). `error` mirrors `message` for callers written against the older bare `{ error }` bodies. `requestId` echoes the `X-Request-Id` response header when the request-id middleware attached one, which it does for every request under `/api/v1/prod`.

code.description: See ErrorCode for the complete list.

details.description: One message per offending field. Absent on non validation 400s.

SearchPagination.title: SearchPagination
SearchPagination.description: Pagination block for keyword search. It is the pagination object returned by the search backend with `hasMore` recomputed by the API layer. Note that `totalPages` is only present on the degraded path where the backend returned no pagination at all, so do not depend on it; use `hasMore` and `nextCursor`.

totalPages.description: Only present on the degraded fallback path.

nextCursor.description: A signed opaque string: send it back verbatim as `cursor` to fetch the next page, or `null` on the last page. This is the shape a self serve tier caller sees. A raw array of OpenSearch sort values is returned instead, for the legacy `searchAfter` contract, only while self serve tiers are off.

EstimatedPagination.title: EstimatedPagination
EstimatedPagination.description: Pagination block for semantic search. `total` and `totalPages` are conservative estimates derived from fetching one extra row, and are exact only on the final page.

query.description: Search terms. Trimmed, and must not be empty after trimming.

court.description: Court name or names, matched verbatim against the index spelling, for example `Bombay High Court`. Comma separated strings are also split.

year.description: Year of decision. Accepts an integer, a 4 digit string, or an array of either. Integers are bounded to 1947 (Indian independence) through the current year.

caseType.description: Case type code or primary type. Primary types such as `Appeal` are expanded server side into their component codes.

caseNumber.description: Exact case number filter, forwarded to the search service. Single valued: a string, or an array of at most one string. An array with more than one entry is rejected with 400.

judgeName.description: Judge name filter. Use `GET /judges/search` to resolve exact spellings.

judges.description: Alias for `judgeName`. Used only when `judgeName` is absent.

judge.description: Alias for `judgeName`. Used only when `judgeName` and `judges` are both absent.

fromDate.description: Inclusive lower bound on decision date, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

toDate.description: Inclusive upper bound on decision date, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

searchAfter.description: Legacy, unsigned deep pagination cursor: JSON encode the `pagination.nextCursor` array from a pre-`cursor` response. Honoured only while self serve tiers are off; a self serve caller should send `cursor` instead, since an unsigned `searchAfter` is not continued from once the tier system is live. A single scalar value is also accepted.

cursor.description: Signed deep pagination cursor (server/utils/signed-cursor.ts). Send the previous response's `pagination.nextCursor` string back verbatim; do not construct or edit one. Carries the exact search position, the paging depth reached so far, and a hash of the query and filters, so it cannot be replayed against a different query or hand-edited past a tier's pagination depth cap. See "Pagination cursors" above.

sortBy.description: Sort order. `relevance` (default), `recent` (newest decision date first) or `oldest`. `date` is a deprecated alias for `recent`, kept so callers written against the old schema keep working; when you send it the response includes a `meta.warnings` entry. `meta.sortBy` reports the sort actually applied.

SemanticSearchRequest.title: SemanticSearchRequest
SemanticSearchRequest.description: The top level filter parameters use the same names as `POST /search/cases` and are mapped onto the vector store keys: `court` to `court`, `year` to `caseYear`, `caseType` to `caseType`, `caseNumber` to `caseNumber`, `judgeName`/`judges`/`judge` to `judgeName`, and `fromDate`/`toDate` to the `decisionDate` range. Precedence, weakest first: filters the model inferred from `query`, then these top level parameters, then the nested `filters` object. `meta.appliedFilters` reports the result.

query.description: Natural language description of what you are looking for. At least 3 characters.
query.example: when can a court lift the corporate veil to hold directors personally liable

court.description: Court name or names, matched against the vector store `court` payload key. A High Court representative name is expanded to its member spellings. Comma separated strings are also split.

year.description: Year of decision. Accepts an integer, a 4 digit string, or an array of either. Integers are bounded to 1947 (Indian independence) through the current year.

caseType.description: Case type code or primary type, mapped to the `caseType` payload key. Primary types such as `Appeal` are expanded server side into their component codes.

caseNumber.description: Case number, digits only, for example `1234`. The vector index stores case numbers as integers, so a value containing anything other than digits is rejected with 400. Use `POST /search/cases` to filter on a full case number string.

judgeName.description: Single judge name, matched against the indexed `judges` values, so it must be the exact indexed spelling. Use `GET /judges/search` to resolve it. A one element array is also accepted; more than one judge is rejected with 400 because the vector store matches one name at a time.

judges.description: Alias for `judgeName`. Used only when `judgeName` is absent.

judge.description: Alias for `judgeName`. Used only when `judgeName` and `judges` are both absent.

fromDate.description: Inclusive lower bound on decision date, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Applied as `decisionDate.$gte`.

toDate.description: Inclusive upper bound on decision date, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Applied as `decisionDate.$lte`.

limit.description: Results per page. The handler additionally clamps this to 100.

filters.description: Vector store filters addressed directly. These take precedence over the top level parameters and over anything the model extracted from `query`. Keys the downstream layer understands: `court`, `courtType`, `courtName`, `caseType`, `caseYear`, `registrationYear`, `decisionYear`, `judgeName`, `caseNumber`, `practiceArea`, `precedentValue`, and `decisionDate` with `$gte` and `$lte` sub keys.

AnalyzeRequest.title: AnalyzeRequest
AnalyzeRequest.description: Body for `POST /cases/{id}/analyze-consolidated`. See AnalyzeCaseRequest for the single-case endpoint, which additionally accepts `allowRemoteFetch`.

force.description: Re run the analysis even when one already exists. Costs credits every time.
Re run the analysis even when one already exists. Costs credits every time.

allowRemoteFetch.description: Required before the analysis will fetch this case's source document from an external host (rather than this app's own S3 storage) when no rawText or S3 object is already available. The target host must still match REMOTE_PDF_HOST_ALLOWLIST regardless of this flag. Adds a flat 20 credit surcharge when a fetch actually runs. See "Fetching a document from outside S3" on the endpoint.

case_id.description: The 24 character MongoDB ObjectId of the case, as returned in the `id` field elsewhere in this API. A case number is not accepted, and a value that is not 24 hexadecimal characters is rejected with 400.

PartyScreenRequest.title: PartyScreenRequest
PartyScreenRequest.description: Mirrors partyScreenSchema (server/utils/api-v1-validations.ts) field for field. `additionalProperties` is not set to false here because the schema itself has no `.strict()` at the top level; `identifiers` and `address` are individually strict.

name.description: The person or company name to screen. Trimmed.

aliases.description: Alternate names to screen alongside `name`. At most 7: the name plus its aliases must fit within the 8 name screening limit.

entityType.description: Required. Drives the confidence model: a `person` can never be auto-confirmed on name evidence alone, see the endpoint description.

purpose.description: Required. Why this name is being screened, per DPDP section 5 grounds. Never logged alongside the name itself, only alongside counts.

identifiers.description: Statutory identifiers. Each is format and check digit validated (server/services/entity-resolution/name-utils.ts) and rejected with 400 if malformed, rather than silently passed through as an unmatchable string. An exact match on any of these is the only way a `person` screen can reach the `confirmed` confidence band.

address.description: A weak corroborating signal, not an identifier: narrows ambiguity on a common name but never alone reaches `confirmed`.

knownPersons.description: Names of directors, officers or known associates. Another corroborating signal, used the same way as `address`.

court.description: Restrict the screen to one or more courts. The internal search service accepts a single court filter, so only the first entry of an array is honoured; this is a documented limitation, not a validation error.

since.description: Only consider cases with a decision or filing date on or after this date, YYYY-MM-DD. Best effort: a case with neither date is kept rather than dropped.

limit.description: Maximum candidates to retrieve before scoring.

adjudicate.description: Run the LLM adjudication pass over the uncertain middle (up to 40 candidates), adding the 80 credit surcharge. See "Pricing" on the endpoint.

displayThreshold.description: Minimum calibrated match probability for a candidate to appear in `matches`, default 0.6. A `confirmed` match is always shown regardless of this threshold.

OpenSearchCaseHit.title: OpenSearchCaseHit
OpenSearchCaseHit.description: A search hit forwarded from the OpenSearch microservice. The API layer does NOT run these through the response sanitizer, and the code types them as `unknown[]`, so the exact field set is not pinned down anywhere in the source. The properties listed below are the ones present on essentially every record across Supreme Court, High Court and District Court ingestion; additional court specific fields may be present. Treat this object as open. `id` is always present (added by the API layer itself, not the OpenSearch microservice) and is the field to read; `_id` and `mongoId` remain on the hit, when the underlying record carries them, only for backward compatibility with integrations built before `id` was added.

id.description: Case identifier, usable as the `{id}` path parameter. Always present.

_id.description: The same identifier as `id`. Kept for backward compatibility; prefer `id`.

mongoId.description: The same identifier as `id`, on records where `_id` is absent. Kept for backward compatibility; prefer `id`.

decisionDate.description: ISO date or date-time, depending on the source record.

CaseListItem.title: CaseListItem
CaseListItem.description: Compact case record returned by semantic search. Undefined fields are stripped, so treat everything except `id` as optional.

similarity.description: Vector similarity score, roughly 0 to 1. Added by the semantic search handler only, and the minimum score threshold is 0.3.

CaseDetails.title: CaseDetails
CaseDetails.description: Case metadata. Undefined fields are stripped, so treat everything except `id` as optional. `detailedSummary`, `headnote`, `holding` and `keyFacts` are deliberately excluded and live on the analysis endpoint.

metadata.description: Present only when the source record carries a diary number.

hasAnalysis.description: True when a stored AI analysis with a summary exists. Fetch it from `/cases/{id}/analysis`.

CaseAnalysisResult.title: CaseAnalysisResult
CaseAnalysisResult.description: When `hasAnalysis` is false the object carries `message` and no `analysis` key.

message.const: AI analysis not available for this case

AnalysisBody.title: AnalysisBody
AnalysisBody.description: The AI analysis. Every property is optional: fields the model did not produce are stripped before the response is sent.

issues.description: Legal issues paired with the court holding on each.

citedCases.description: Cited authorities bucketed by how this judgment treated them.

StoredAnalysis.title: StoredAnalysis
StoredAnalysis.description: The analysis object as stored, returned by the two analyze endpoints. It is passed through `sanitizeAnalysis`, which only strips the internal `analysisModel`, `analysisVersion`, `analysisDate` and `analysisMethod` fields, so it is a superset of `AnalysisBody`: it also carries `outcome`, `benchComposition`, `opinionType`, `factPattern` and `linkedCases`. Every property is optional.

relatedDocuments.description: Documents sharing this case number, newest first, capped at 50.

isCurrent.description: True for the document you asked about.

timeline.description: Chronological procedural events, oldest first. Only documents that have both a decision date and a stored PDF appear here, so this is usually shorter than `relatedDocuments`.

status.description: Derived from the document case type and disposal nature. The earliest entry is relabelled `Case Initiated` unless it is already a `Final Judgment`.

statusLabel.description: The disposal nature when present, otherwise the same value as `status`.

pdfUrl.description: An encrypted presigned S3 URL. It is NOT directly fetchable: decrypt it client side with the case specific key first.

expiresIn.description: Lifetime of the underlying presigned URL in seconds.

cached.description: Present when the response was served from orders already fetched today.

message.description: Human readable context, present on cached and short circuit paths.

orders.description: Order records, present only when orders were already available. The order document shape is assembled dynamically from the source court record and is not typed in the source, so treat each entry as an open object.

result.description: Generic job result. Included only when `totalOrderCount` is absent, so that there is one representation of the orders rather than two. Untyped in the source.

orders.description: Fetched orders. Untyped in the source, treat each entry as an open object.

totalOrderCount.description: Orders known for the case overall.

MatchSignal.title: MatchSignal
MatchSignal.description: One piece of evidence the confidence score was built from.

name.description: What this signal checks, for example `pan`, `name_similarity`, `address_city`.

evidence.description: The exact input token(s) this signal is grounded in. No information from outside the request or the candidate case.

PartyScreenCaseFields.title: PartyScreenCaseFields
PartyScreenCaseFields.description: Plain case fields shared by every entry in `matches` and `relatedButUnverified`. Undefined fields are stripped, so treat everything except `caseId` as optional.

caseId.description: Usable as the `{id}` path parameter on the case endpoints.

PartyScreenMatch.title: PartyScreenMatch
PartyScreenMatch.description: One scored candidate. See the endpoint description for what the confidence bands mean and the rule that a person is never auto-confirmed on name evidence alone.

partyRole.description: The searched party's apparent role in this case.

score.description: Alias of `calibrated`, kept as a stable top level "the number" field.

engine.description: `llm` only when `adjudicate: true` was requested and the model actually reviewed this candidate.

strategies.description: Which retrieval strategies surfaced this candidate.

nameSimilarity.description: Best name similarity between the searched name (or an alias) and this candidate.

disambiguatorPresent.description: Whether an identifier, address or known-person disambiguator was available for this candidate, not just a bare name.

rationale.description: Present when the deterministic core or the LLM produced an explanation.

exhaustive.description: The retrieval covered the full corpus for this name.

exhaustiveWithinFilters.description: The retrieval covered the full corpus within the filters given (`court`, `since`), even if not the whole corpus.

planClamped.description: The account's plan limited how much retrieval this call could do.

anyStrategyErrored.description: At least one retrieval strategy failed; the run is not exhaustive even if others succeeded.

someRecordsWithheld.description: A case was dropped because it is restricted under the case removal policy, or its title carried a masking token. This is the ONLY disclosure made about withheld records: never a count, an id, or which candidate it was. See "Restricted records" above.

verdict.description: `no_matches_found` only when the retrieval was exhaustive; otherwise `inconclusive`. See "The verdict and exhaustiveness" on the endpoint.

query.description: Echo of the request as it was actually applied, including defaulted fields (`limit`, `adjudicate`, `displayThreshold`).

relatedButUnverified.description: Candidates the search layer surfaced but that did not clear the scoring floor. Plain case fields only, no confidence, evidence, partyRole or rationale.

adjudicationsRun.description: How many candidates the LLM actually reviewed on this call, always 0 when `adjudicate` was false.

notice.description: Standing notice about the case removal policy and what a no-match verdict does and does not mean, included on every response.

PartyScreenBatchItem.title: PartyScreenBatchItem
PartyScreenBatchItem.description: One screen inside a batch call. Same fields as PartyScreenRequest except `purpose` (given once at the batch top level) and `adjudicate` (fixed false for the whole batch).

clientRef.description: Your own identifier for this item, echoed back verbatim on the matching result so you can join it to your own records without CourtMesh needing to understand your identifiers.

entityType.description: Overrides the batch top level `entityType` for this item. Required, on this item or at the top level, one way or another.

identifiers.description: Same shape and validation as PartyScreenRequest.identifiers.

purpose.description: Required, given once for the whole batch. Same DPDP section 5 grounds requirement as PartyScreenRequest.purpose.

entityType.description: Default for every item that does not set its own `entityType`. An item with neither its own nor this default is a per-item validation error.

adjudicate.description: Must be `false` (or omitted) for a batch call: adjudication is single-item only, on POST /party/screen directly.

PartyScreenBatchItemResult.title: PartyScreenBatchItemResult
PartyScreenBatchItemResult.description: One entry in data.results per admitted item, in admission order (which is request order, minus anything the distinct-names cap truncated away - see the endpoint description). `index` still names each result's original position in the request's `items` array.

code.description: Always this one fixed value today: the batch runner does not yet distinguish failure reasons per item.

clientRef.description: Echo of the item's own `clientRef`. Absent when the item did not send one.

index.description: The item's 0 based position in the request's `items` array.

businessDaysBehind.description: Business days between the latest indexed decision and today. Null when it cannot be computed.

DistrictCourtsRollup.title: DistrictCourtsRollup
DistrictCourtsRollup.description: One rolled up row for every District Court combined: the index carries no state field to break this down further today.

generatedAt.description: When this snapshot was computed, not when this response was served (the snapshot may be served stale from cache).

index.description: The OpenSearch index name this snapshot was computed from.

courts.description: High Courts and tribunals, one row each.
